targets.target: Twitch Channel Points and creator Custom Rewards
targets.finding: Viewers earn channel-specific Channel Points while watching and redeem rewards configured by the creator. The queue flow should use a dedicated Custom Reward created for that queue by this bot; ordinary existing rewards such as drink-water are separate.

targets.target: Twitch Channel Points custom rewards eligibility
targets.finding: Create Custom Rewards requires channel:manage:redemptions and Twitch returns 403 when the broadcaster is not Affiliate or Partner.
The subscription requires user:read:chat from the chatting user; its condition binds broadcaster_user_id and user_id. The reference does not list an Affiliate/Partner requirement for this chat event.

targets.target: Installed Twitch chat clients and WebSocket EventSub
targets.finding: Twitch documents installed chatbots using the broadcaster's user access token; reading requires user:read:chat and sending optionally/for this product requires user:write:chat. WebSocket EventSub is recommended for end-user-hosted chatbots.

apps/api/src/twitch/integration.mjs stops auth and returns before EventSub construction when getChannelEligibility reports ineligible. apps/api/src/twitch/auth-runtime.mjs requires channel:manage:redemptions plus user:read:chat and user:write:chat for every token. The EventSub chat callback and queue add command already exist; addManualEntry persists source=manual with no redemption id and no financial intent.

targets.target: Existing reward ownership and unrelated custom rewards
targets.finding: Queue reward lifecycle must remain restricted to the app-managed reward ID. A pre-existing drink-water reward is unrelated and must not be paused, adopted, fulfilled, or deleted by queue setup.
targets.status: verified_constraint; behavior will receive a regression test

targets.target: Twitch Custom Reward creation, ownership, and redemption recovery
targets.finding: Helix can list rewards with only_manageable_rewards=false, but only the creating app may retrieve redemption records; reward updates, redemption status changes, and deletion are also tied to creator ownership. Support bot-created rewards by default. A dashboard-created reward may be selected only if an authorized test proves this Client ID can perform every lifecycle operation the product requires, including pause/open, pending and individual redemption retrieval/reconciliation, cancel/fulfill, and safe deletion after pending redemptions are resolved.
targets.status: official documentation reviewed 2026-10-07; end-to-end Dashboard reward test pending

targets.target: Twitch Monetization for All and Channel Points availability
targets.finding: Current Twitch documentation says Channel Points are available to monetized streamers after completing creator onboarding; availability can no longer be inferred only from Affiliate/Partner status. The operator reports successfully creating a reward in the Creator Dashboard while not Affiliate, which is reported evidence of Dashboard access, not evidence that this app can use the API.
targets.status: official documentation reviewed 2026-10-07; Dashboard access reported by operator; API untested

targets.target: Creator Dashboard reward visibility versus Helix ownership
targets.finding: GET /helix/channel_points/custom_rewards can list rewards with only_manageable_rewards=false; true limits results to rewards manageable by the Client ID. The reference says only the creating app may retrieve redemptions, update the reward, update redemption status, or delete the reward. EventSub delivery does not prove full recovery/management capability. The API still documents 403 for non-Affiliate/Partner broadcasters on Custom Reward endpoints, conflicting with expanded product availability.
targets.status: official documentation reviewed 2026-10-07; authorized end-to-end test pending

inference: Since Twitch documents chat EventSub scopes/conditions without an Affiliate/Partner gate while the Channel Points create endpoint explicitly has that gate, chat may be usable independently for a non-affiliate broadcaster. This is an inference from the separate contracts and still needs a controlled real-channel acceptance check before claiming it works end to end.

The implementation now probes the actual Helix reward endpoint rather than relying on broadcasterType, preserves OAuth/chat runtime and command authorization when that probe is unsupported, and conditionally disables reward subscriptions, workers, and reconciliation. Adapter and integration tests cover the result mapping and chat continuity; authorized live OAuth/EventSub/chat acceptance and full reward lifecycle proof remain pending.

Using an arbitrary pre-existing custom reward as a queue trigger would allow event observation but would not provide the required Helix redemption recovery and status control for a different Client ID; this conflicts with the product reliability and financial-audit requirements.

Capability decisions should use actual authorized results of the required Helix operations, not broadcasterType alone or Dashboard visibility. Transient network/auth failures must be distinguished from definitive unavailability to avoid silently downgrading a queue already linked to a reward.
unverifiedClaims: No authorized non-affiliate channel has been tested with the installed EventSub chat flow in this repository.
The exact Twitch OAuth token validation policy for an ineligible channel when channel:manage:redemptions is absent has not been exercised against Twitch.
Live messages and replies from an ineligible channel have not been tested.
It has not been tested whether this bot Client ID can retrieve history, reconcile missed redemptions, and update the status of a reward manually created in Creator Dashboard.
